criteria.description: FB-26: the trail sampler asserts hue lock within 10 degrees, deltaE*ab no greater than 8 against the payload-derived expectation from rampForReturn(holding.dayReturn) (not rampForWeekly / weeklyReturn), and ordering across same-direction holdings - for every holding in the fixture, sampled at each holding's own naturally unoccluded orbital phase. Literal-hex baselines survive only for flat, comet and sun tokens.

implementer.notes: Owner ruling implemented (2026-07-30, "sampler searches for a valid point; no threshold moves"): the single fixed TRAIL_SAMPLE_FRACTION=0.62 is replaced by a per-holding positional search. scene-model.ts now exports TRAIL_SAMPLE_SEARCH_FRACTIONS (an ordered walk outward from 0.62 in 0.08 steps, clamped to [0.2, 0.92]); OrreryScene.tsx projects every candidate fraction each frame and publishes them as data-trail-sample-candidates (JSON array of {fraction, x, y}), alongside the unchanged single data-trail-sample-x/y for back-compat. sample-live-rgb.mjs now walks a ticker's full candidate list within each sampled frame (combined with the pre-existing per-frame temporal search) and accepts the first candidate that clears the EXISTING, UNCHANGED gates (deltaE<=8, hueDistance<=10, chroma>0.3, clearance>=1px) -- no threshold, ramp, clamp or arc constant was touched. Fresh live run against a rebuilt production server (150s window, 137 frames, up to 1507 candidates tried for a single ticker): 7/8 now pass (GOOG 0.598, COST 7.785, MSFT 1.572, INTC 1.398, IBM 6.674, CBRS 2.757, CRM 7.786), up from 3/8 before this fix. The 3 previously-passing tickers (GOOG, IBM, CRM) still pass, per the owner's explicit requirement. COST -- previously landing on the ribbon's antialiased edge -- now passes at fraction 0.54 (deltaE 7.785, clearance 27.357px). ASML remains a genuine reportable failure, not a silent skip, exactly as the ruling anticipated: 1507 candidates were tried across every frame and every fraction in the full [0.2, 0.92] search range over 137 frames (~137s), and none cleared the deltaE<=8 gate (best found: deltaE 9.436, clearance 5.115px -- clearance meaningfully improved from the pre-fix best of 3.783px, but the sun-corona/own-disc colour contamination this section's F2 investigation measured is structural to ASML's tight-orbit/large-disc geometry and was not resolved by moving the sample point alone). MSFT/INTC/CBRS's prior clamp-collision cause (three holdings pinned to the identical brightest ramp stop, additive-glow bleed) is fully resolved by the walk -- a different fraction moves the sample off the point where the glow pass's own overlap was brightest, without touching the clamp/ramp itself. One new, small, honestly-reported side effect: the magnitude-ordering check now shows one violation (zero before this fix) -- GOOG (deltaE 0.598, near-perfect sample) and COST (deltaE 7.785, a passing but comparatively imprecise sample) are adjacent in the sorted loss-magnitude order with different expected ramp stops; COST's measured luminance (0.460382) is marginally higher (+0.003) than GOOG's (0.457404), inverting the expected monotonic ordering by an amount consistent with COST's own sampling imprecision rather than an encoding defect. Not corrected here -- doing so would mean further tuning the search order/parameters to chase one ticker's exact pixel, which is the same kind of unbounded, unauthorized methodology tinkering the owner's ruling forbids ('no threshold moves'). Reported per the ruling's own instruction ('if the search alters their results, that gets reported rather than accepted') rather than hidden or silently reconciled. docs/phase10-baseline/section-13/raw-trail-sampler-TST-03.json and trail-daily-1440x900.png were regenerated by this run; the round-2 f2-investigation evidence is retained as the still-valid root-cause record for ASML's residual failure and COST's now-resolved prior failure.

reviewer.notes: Round 4: Devan ruled on the narrower question round 3 routed to him (commit f392a049d4a4a9e49dda1404890d5941b00040ff, 'phase10(owner §13): ASML exception; Chart Room promoted to its own §14'). GRANTED a documented, non-generalizing exception for ASML on TST-03 only -- deltaE 9.436 against the unweakened <=8 gate, reproduced identically across three independent runs (the implementer's and two of the reviewer's, one written from scratch). Cause: ASML orbits nearest the sun and the sun's light falls on its ribbon, shifting the measured colour past tolerance; the renderer is arguably correct and the criterion does not model scene illumination. He was explicit this is NOT the carried_by_owner path he refused in round 3 ('carry means still-broken, fix-it-later, and defers the same problem forward; this is understood-and-accepted, cause named, measurement attached, and it does not travel to another section') -- the status recorded here is `carried_by_owner` only because that is the acceptance ledger's mechanical status for an owner-authorized pass on a residual failure (per scripts/phase10-workflow-lib.mjs's own comment, 'carried_by_owner is the lane for taste/owner verdicts'); the substance is a scoped exception, not a deferral, and PHASE10_STATE.json's section.owner_exceptions carries the full ruling verbatim. Scope: ASML only, TST-03 only -- the <=8 gate remains unweakened for every other holding, present and future, and GOOG/IBM/CRM continue to pass (re-confirmed this round: candidate unchanged at 33789ee, git diff --name-only 33789ee HEAD -- src/ public/ package.json package-lock.json scripts/ is empty, and this turn's own fresh npm test/npm run build runs matched round 3's exactly). INTC's flakiness (2/3 runs pass, 1/3 misses narrowly at 8.81) is logged by the owner as a non-blocking observation, almost certainly ASML's cause at lower magnitude, and does not gate this criterion. The stale rootCauseFinding prose noted in round 3 remains a cosmetic nit, not corrected this turn (out of scope for an acceptance-only turn).

criteria.description: FB-17: --panel-width default changes from 460px to 600px. A capture of the live production default (no query params, real npm run build && npm run start) at 1440x900 shows the panel at 600px, plus a written, measured explanation of the live/capture size disagreement the owner reported, covering panel width measured across a realistic range of viewport widths (1280/1366/1440/1536/1920) and browser zoom as a candidate cause.

implementer.notes: Live production default (npm run build && npm run start, no query params) renders the approach panel at exactly 600px across all five tested viewport widths (1280/1366/1440/1536/1920), all at devicePixelRatio 2. The calc(100vw - 3rem) responsive floor does not bind at any tested width (100vw-3rem >= 1232px, well above 600px), so viewport width alone does not reproduce the owner's live/capture disagreement. Leading remaining candidate per the investigation: non-100% browser zoom, which shrinks the effective CSS pixel viewport the same way a narrower window would but cannot be simulated by Playwright's viewport option. The calc() floor itself was not changed -- it is a genuine constraint, not a bug -- since the investigation did not find a units/precedence defect.

reviewer.notes: Independently re-measured panel width at all five viewports (1280/1366/1440/1536/1920) against a fresh production server: exactly 600px at every width, confirming the calc(100vw - 3rem) floor does not bind in this range, matching the implementer's own finding. Evidence list corrected round 4 to also cite the rendered capture (panel-width-live-default.png) alongside the raw measurement JSON -- round 1-3 cited the JSON only, an evidence-hygiene gap caught by node scripts/phase10-acceptance.mjs check --require reviewer this round, not a change in the underlying finding.

criteria.description: FB-22: a 1440x900 overview capture shows no unexplained yellow/gold haze or glow above the sun, with the implementer's notes naming the actual identified cause among the aurora mesh, the glow shells, or the docking ring.

implementer.notes: Root-caused via live capture and pixel sampling directly above the sun's projected center (not guessed): a vertical pixel scan straight up from the sun found bright yellow/gold values (e.g. rgb(251,229,101), rgb(244,172,77)) 20-100px above the sun's disc edge, matching a visible soft yellow glow bulging above the sphere in the crop. This is the aurora mesh (candidate a) -- at the overview camera's elevated, forward-offset angle, its prior position (yInOuterRadii 0.92, zInOuterRadii -0.72) placed it close enough behind the sun in screen projection to visually merge with its silhouette. Fixed by repositioning it further up/back (yInOuterRadii 1.65, zInOuterRadii -1.35) -- opacity/formula (raised by FB-02 in this same section) was deliberately left untouched since the owner wants the aurora reliably visible, not hidden. Re-captured after the fix: the same vertical scan and crop show a clean sun silhouette with no haze. Not the glow shells (symmetric full-sphere, opacity too low at rest to read as a distinct shape) or the docking ring (hover-only, only visible on interaction, and full 360 degrees rather than a semi-circle).

reviewer.notes: Reviewed a fresh overview capture from a freshly built production server: clean sun silhouette, no yellow/gold haze above it.
